# Artisan: An Agentic Approach for Artifact Evaluation

## Installation

Artisan uses three kinds of Docker containers:

* A Visual Studio Code Dev Container for running Artisan itself. See [devcontainer.json](.devcontainer/devcontainer.json).

* Docker-outside-docker containers for running OpenHands docker runtime.

* Docker containers for running the docker images for research artifacts.

To install and run Artisan, follow these steps:

1) Install [Visual Studio Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/download) and its ["Dev Containers" extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-vscode-remote.remote-containers).

2) Set up the api key for LLMS by setting API_KEY and OPENAI_API_KEY environment variables to the api provider of your choice.

## Running the benchmark

Run on the whole benchmark
```sh
uv run artisan reprobench
```

Run specific paper 
```sh
uv run artisan reprobench -f pythonic
```

Run specific table of the paper
```sh
uv run artisan reprobench -f pythonic-t2
```

Run with multiple workers 
```sh
uv run artisan reprobench -w 8 -f pythonic-t2
```

Run with repetitions
```sh
uv run artisan reprobench -r 8 -f pythonic-t2
```

## Testing single reproduction script

First you have to run the judging server:

```sh
uv run artisan judge
```

Then, in a separate terminal, you can test a single reproduction script:

```sh
uv run artisan submit evaluation/scripts/pythonic_table_2.sh
vscode ➜ /workspaces/artisan (main) $ uv run artisan submit evaluation/scripts/pythonic_table_2.sh 
Submitting to judge service at http://localhost:8000/submit...
```
